exercises.prompt: How is the definite article (الـ) pronounced in الشَّمْسُ?
exercises.explanation: ش is a solar letter (ḥarf shamsī), so the lām of the definite article (الـ) assimilates completely into ش, which is pronounced doubled (shaddah): ash-shamsu.

feedback.rule: Solar letters assimilate the lām of the definite article (الـ) and take shaddah.
feedback.commonError: Pronouncing the lām before a solar letter or omitting the shaddah.

exercises.prompt: True or False: In الشَّمْسُ وَالقَمَرُ, the hamzat al-waṣl of القَمَرُ is pronounced as a glottal stop after وَ.
exercises.explanation: False. Hamzat al-waṣl elides after a preceding vowel, so وَالقَمَرُ is read continuously as wa-l-qamaru.

feedback.rule: Hamzat al-waṣl drops in connected reading when preceded by a vowel.
feedback.commonError: Pronouncing wa-ʾal-qamaru as if it were hamzat al-qaṭʿ.

exercises.prompt: Match each orthographic sign to its phonetic function.
exercises.explanation: Shaddah doubles a consonant, sukūn marks absence of a vowel, and maddah marks long ā after hamzah.

exercises.prompt: Active Recall: Type the Arabic word for 'the sun' with the definite article (with or without tashkīl):
exercises.explanation: The word for 'the sun' is الشَّمْسُ. Notice that because ش is a solar letter, in pronunciation the lām assimilates, giving ash-shamsu.

feedback.rule: Solar assimilation doubles the solar letter (shaddah) after the definite article (الـ).
feedback.commonError: Remember to write the lām in script even though it assimilates in pronunciation.
